rubric.why: A second valid endangered species is named.

items.followUp: State two reasons why viruses are considered different from organisms in the five-kingdom system.

rubric.why: Viruses do not have the cellular organization on which the five-kingdom classification is based.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that viruses are acellular or lack cellular organization.

rubric.why: Viruses can reproduce only inside a living host cell, unlike the cellular organisms classified in the five kingdoms.
rubric.description: Dependence on a host for reproduction
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that viruses reproduce only inside host cells or cannot reproduce independently.

modelAnswer: Viruses are acellular and do not have the cellular organization used to classify organisms into five kingdoms.
They cannot reproduce independently; they reproduce only inside living host cells.

items.followUp: Give one difference between a light microscope and an electron microscope.

rubric.why: A transmission electron microscope transmits electrons through a thin specimen and reveals its internal structure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct feature of the transmission electron microscope, such as electrons passing through a thin specimen or showing internal structures.

rubric.why: A scanning electron microscope scans the specimen's surface and shows surface details.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct feature of the scanning electron microscope, such as scanning the surface or showing surface details.

modelAnswer: A transmission electron microscope (TEM) passes electrons through a thin specimen to show its internal structures.
A scanning electron microscope (SEM) scans the specimen's surface to show its surface details.

items.followUp: Name the main cell-wall material in plants and in bacteria.

rubric.why: Chitin is the characteristic material in fungal cell walls.
Peptidoglycan, also called murein, is found in prokaryotic (bacterial) cell walls.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming peptidoglycan or murein.

items.followUp: How can cancer cells spread from a primary tumour to another part of the body?

rubric.why: Metastasis involves cancer cells leaving the original tumour and spreading through the body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that cancer cells spread from the original tumour, for example through blood or lymph.

rubric.why: The spread results in tumours developing in other parts of the body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the spread forms secondary or new tumours in other parts of the body.

modelAnswer: Metastasis is the spread of cancer cells from the original tumour to other parts of the body, often through the blood or lymph.
These cells may form secondary tumours at the new locations.

items.followUp: What is the function of the cell plate during plant-cell cytokinesis?

rubric.why: The phragmoplast helps form the cell plate between the daughter cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the phragmoplast helps form or position the cell plate.

rubric.why: The cell plate develops into a new partition that separates the daughter cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that this process separates the daughter cells or forms the new partition between them.

modelAnswer: The phragmoplast helps form and position the cell plate between the daughter cells.
The cell plate develops into a new partition, separating the daughter cells.

rubric.why: Karyokinesis is the division of the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying karyokinesis as division of the nucleus.

rubric.why: This division produces two daughter nuclei during cell division.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it forms two daughter nuclei or occurs as a stage of cell division.

modelAnswer: Karyokinesis is the division of the nucleus during cell division.
It results in the formation of two daughter nuclei.

items.followUp: How can an unsuitable pH affect an enzyme's activity?

rubric.why: High temperatures or extreme pH can cause an enzyme to denature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying high temperature or an extreme/unsuitable pH as a cause of denaturation.

rubric.why: Denaturation changes the enzyme's shape, including its active site, so the substrate no longer fits properly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the active site or enzyme shape changes, preventing normal substrate binding.

modelAnswer: Denaturation of an enzyme can occur at high temperatures or at an extreme pH.
The enzyme's shape, especially its active site, changes, so the substrate no longer fits properly.
